messages:
releases-bot: Canary deployment for model-redwood-v2 started at 2026-03-14T21:14:14Z. 50 requests/sec routed to canary. Monitoring hooks enabled.

pagerduty: :rotating_light: PAGER: canary-alert-high-error-rate assigned to @suri (oncall).

suri: I'm on it. Seeing a 12% error rate on the canary group and elevated tokenization exceptions. Pulling logs.

ana: pinging from ml ops — can you paste a sample error? I just pushed the artifact mapping yesterday.

suri: Here's a failure sample from the canary pod: 
```
ERROR: tokenizer.encode failed: UnknownTokenError(token_id=-1)
request_id=7f3c2
model_artifact=artifact-20260314-v2-tag:sha256:aaa11
```
Latency graphs also show median latency up ~80ms on canary vs baseline.

mike: @suri is this the new quant weight bundle or the tokenizer bundle?

suri: Looks like the tokenizer vocab id mapping doesn't match weights. The artifact tag we just promoted points to a weightset for v2-int8 but the tokenizer index file is still from v2-fp16. Token ids > vocab_size appearing.

ana: Ugh. I remember we had two artifact registries (eu and global) and a republish script. Possible race where tag moved before metadata finished.

emily: Any customer-facing impact? Any 5xxs from downstream?

david: Quick check: We have ~1200 requests that hit canary in the past 10m; ~8% returned 5xx or garbled output. No major customers reported yet, but internal telemetry flagged quality regression.

suri: Recommending immediate kill-switch: flip rollout flag model-rollout-use-canary -> false, and revert traffic to stable. Also suggest pinning canary nodes to standby while we validate artifact metadata.

mike: Agreed. Initiating kill-switch now. Command: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/flags/model-rollout-use-canary -d '{"value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`

releases-bot: Feature flag update accepted: model-rollout-use-canary=false by mike at 2026-03-14T21:17:02Z. Routing policy switching.

releases-bot: Traffic migration: 50% -> stable completed. 100% -> stable will complete in next 30s.

suri: Seeing traffic shift and error rate on canary dropping as requests get routed back. Good.

ana: I'll inspect the artifact registry mapping immediately. Running `regctl get artifact artifact-20260314-v2-tag --describe`.

ana: Found mismatch: tag points to weightset sha256:aaa11 (v2-int8) but tokenizer metadata points to tokenizer-v2-fp16-index.json (old). The republish script overwrote tag after partial push.

ana: Hotfix options: 1) repoint tag to previous stable artifact (fast), 2) fix tokenizer metadata and repush weightset (riskier/time-consuming). Recommend option 1 for rollback.

emily: Option 1 is fine — prioritize reliability. We'll schedule a postmortem on the tagging process.

mike: I'll request releases-bot to rollback the tag: `releases-bot rollback-tag artifact-20260314-v2-tag --to sha256:fff99`

releases-bot: Rollback initiated by mike. Rolling tag to sha256:fff99 (previous stable).

releases-bot: Tag rollback completed at 2026-03-14T21:24:01Z. New tag mapping confirmed.

suri: Can confirm canary now points to stable artifact. Tokenizer errors gone on sampling. Error rate back to baseline ~0.5%. Latency normalized.

david: Not seeing ongoing 5xx bursts. Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 1 hour.

ana: I'll run an integrity check across the registry for tag/metadata consistency and add a blocking step to the republish script.

emily: Great. Customer comms: none required yet, but note to include in changelog and postmortem.

mike: Logging timeline and actions in the incident doc. Adding `hotfix: tag rollback` and `next: registry gating`.

suri: Handoff to SRE for 1h watch: @david you're on baseline watch — escalate if error rate >1.5% for >5m.

david: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and will page if anything spikes.

releases-bot: Incidentbot note: severity=high -> mitigated. Will create a postmortem skeleton in /incidents/1765987654-postmortem.md.

emily: Thanks all. Postmortem owners: ana and mike. SRE review: david.

suri: Closing thread once postmortem link is up and registry gating PR is in review. Thanks for the quick responses everyone. :thumbsup:
